summary: In this lecture, Sheikh Ali Mashhour returns after a personal absence due to family hardship to discuss a fundamental Islamic concept from Zadul-Ma'ad: divine decree and predestination. Using the example of his mother's fall as a teaching moment, he explains the hadith about the creation of the pen 50,000 years before creation, where Allah commanded it to write everything that would occur until the Day of Resurrection. The sheikh elaborates on the Islamic doctrine that while Allah's knowledge encompasses and decrees all events, humans retain free will—a reconciliation between divine omniscience and human agency that is foundational to Islamic theology.
